case_name: Association Of Old Settlers Of Sikkim vs Union Of India

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Association of Old Settlers of Sikkim and Others

facts_of_case: The petitioners prayed for striking down Section 10(26AAA) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, which excludes Indians who settled in Sikkim prior to its merger with India on April 26, 1975. They also sought to strike down the proviso that excludes 'Sikkimese women' who marry a non-Sikkimese after April 1, 2008.

legal_principles.principle: Arbitrary, discriminatory and violative of Article 14 of the Constitution is ultra vires.
legal_principles.held: being arbitrary, discriminatory and violative of Article 14 of the Constitution

legal_principles.principle: A provision that is arbitrary, discriminatory and violative of Articles 14 and 15 of the Constitution is ultra vires.
legal_principles.held: the proviso in Section 10 (26AAA) of the I.T. Act, 1961 is arbitrary, discriminatory and violative of Articles 14 and 15 of the Constitution

outcome.final_order: The court struck down Section 10(26AAA) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, to the extent it excludes Indians who settled in Sikkim prior to its merger with India on April 26, 1975.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
